review.summary: Jaguar TCS Racing lead on 288 points with a comfortable margin at the top. Their two drivers both sit in the top six, with Mitch Evans ahead at 160 and António Félix Da Costa on 128. The points are spread between them rather than carried by one driver, though neither has yet taken a win or podium.

Porsche sit second on 271 points, some distance behind the leading team. Pascal Wehrlein is their standout, sitting at the summit of the drivers' standings on 169, while Nico Müller trails further back in ninth with 102. There is a clear gap between the two, and neither has yet reached a podium.

Mahindra are third on 252 points, holding a clean gap to the teams behind. Edoardo Mortara leads their pair at fifth with 137, and Nyck De Vries is close behind in seventh on 115. Their drivers compare more closely than most of the field, though both remain without a win or podium.

Andretti are fourth on 229 points. Jake Dennis is well placed at second among the drivers on 164, but there is a large divide with teammate Felipe Drugovich in fourteenth on just 65. The team's points rest heavily on Dennis, and neither driver has yet taken a podium.

Citroën sit fifth on 182 points. Nick Cassidy leads the pair at eighth with 114, while Jean-Éric Vergne is further back in twelfth on 68. Cassidy carries most of the team's tally, and there remains a gap between the two drivers that neither has closed with a win or podium.

Nissan are sixth on 157 points. Oliver Rowland is their clear lead driver, sitting fourth among the competitors on 137, whereas Norman Nato sits much lower in nineteenth with just 20. The team's points come almost entirely from Rowland, and there is a wide spread between the two drivers.

Envision are seventh on 152 points. Sébastien Buemi leads the pair at tenth with 97, and Joel Eriksson is further down in sixteenth on 55. The points divide reasonably between them but neither has produced a win or podium, keeping them mid-table behind the leading three teams.

Cupra Kiro are eighth on 128 points. Josep Maria Martí edges ahead of teammate Dan Ticktum, 66 to 62, and the two sit close together in thirteenth and fifteenth. It is a tightly matched pair with neither having yet reached a podium or taken a win.

DS Penske are ninth on 91 points. Taylor Barnard leads the pair at eleventh with 68, while Maximilian Günther sits much lower in eighteenth on just 23. The team's points come largely from Barnard, and there is a clear gap between the two drivers.
